{"findings":[{"rule_id":"WPM-003","evidence":[{"kind":"note","ref":"N3","page":1,"quote":"HEAT TREATMENT NOTE :-
1) TO BE CASE HARDENED UPTO 56~60 HRC.
2) CASE DEPTH 0.8~1.2mm.
3) THREADS TO BE KEEP SOFT.
4) RETAPPING TO BE DONE AFTER SURFACE TREATMENT AT SUPPLIER END.( IF APPLICABLE )"}],"comment":"Note N3 specifies case hardening with a case depth but no area on the drawing is marked to show where the hardened zone applies, leaving the heat treater without guidance. The designer should add hatching or a boundary line (XXXXX) on the views to define the area to be case hardened.","recommended_correction":"Add a clearly marked boundary or cross-hatched zone on the drawing views indicating the exact areas that require case hardening."},{"rule_id":"MF-005","evidence":[{"kind":"title_block","ref":"heat_treatment","page":1,"quote":"---"},{"kind":"note","ref":"N3","page":1,"quote":"HEAT TREATMENT NOTE :-
1) TO BE CASE HARDENED UPTO 56~60 HRC.
2) CASE DEPTH 0.8~1.2mm.
3) THREADS TO BE KEEP SOFT.
4) RETAPPING TO BE DONE AFTER SURFACE TREATMENT AT SUPPLIER END.( IF APPLICABLE )"}],"comment":"The title block field 'heat_treatment' reads '---', contradicting note N3 which requires case hardening to 56–60 HRC, and neither specifies at what manufacturing stage the treatment applies. This ambiguity can cause the part to be shipped untreated or treated at the wrong process step. The designer should update the title block to reference the heat treatment and add the required stage in note N3.","recommended_correction":"Change the title block heat_treatment field from '---' to reference note N3, and revise note N3 to state when the case hardening is to be performed (e.g., after rough machining, before final grinding)."},{"rule_id":"TL-014","evidence":[{"kind":"dimension","ref":"D14","page":1,"quote":"⌀ 50 H7 +0.025"},{"kind":"title_block","ref":"title","page":1,"quote":"BEARING HSG"}],"comment":"The ⌀50 H7 bore (D14) is the bearing seat of this bearing housing, yet no runout control is specified relative to the bearing axis for the rotating assembly's mating features. Without runout, the bearing may be misaligned during operation, causing premature wear or vibration. The designer should add a circular or total runout GD&T callout referencing the bearing bore axis.","recommended_correction":"Apply a runout tolerance on the relevant housing features (such as the outer diameter or mounting face) relative to datum established by the ⌀50 H7 bearing bore."}]}
